about.title: Ukiah Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Ukiah's most recent complete year of public crash data shows 48 injury collisions and 53 people hurt on local roads, with Tuesday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. showing up most often in the reports. Corridors like N and S State Street, Talmage Road, and Airport Park Boulevard carry the bulk of Ukiah's daily traffic, and that volume is reflected in the collision counts. If you were injured in one of these crashes, the days right after matter — insurance adjusters move fast, and evidence like skid marks, dashcam footage, or a damaged bumper can disappear or get repaired before anyone documents it. LawProactive isn't a law firm; we're a free service that connects injured Ukiah residents with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate your situation and explain your options. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no upfront cost to find out where you stand.

whyChoose.title: What Matters Most After a Ukiah Car Accident

items.title: The Clock Is Running
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the crash date to file a car accident claim, but that window shrinks to as little as six months if a government vehicle or agency was involved — which matters if the crash happened near a city-maintained road like Airport Park Boulevard.

items.title: Fault Doesn't Have to Be Black and White
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the crash — your compensation is simply adjusted to reflect your share of fault.

items.title: Be Careful What You Say to the Other Insurer
items.desc: You're not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company, and doing so early on can be used against you later. An attorney can communicate on your behalf so nothing you say gets twisted into a reason to reduce your claim.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Ukiah?
items.answer: In most California car accident cases, you have two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit. If a government entity, like the City of Ukiah or Caltrans, was involved — for example, a poorly maintained stretch of road — that deadline can shrink to as little as six months, so it's worth getting an attorney's input quickly.

items.question: Should I talk to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: You're allowed to decline a recorded statement, and it's often smart to do so before speaking with an attorney. Insurers sometimes use early recorded statements to find inconsistencies or minimize your injuries. An independent attorney connected through LawProactive can handle those conversations for you.

items.question: What if my crash happened on Talmage Road or another busy Ukiah corridor?
items.answer: High-traffic corridors like Talmage Road, N and S State Street, and Airport Park Boulevard see more reported collisions simply because of the volume of vehicles using them, especially during the Tuesday afternoon peak. Documentation from the scene — photos, witness names, and any available footage — can be especially valuable when multiple factors contribute to a crash on a busy road.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and the independent attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only collect a fee if you recover compensation. There's no upfront cost to get matched and discuss your situation.
